title: Running another script is an in-process isolate, not a subprocess
scope:
the `spawn script` construct, `nvs-host`'s isolation boundary, the value-crossing rules, the
`script.spawn` capability, per-tree limit accounting

summary.headline: Running another script starts a sandbox, not a second process
summary.body:
One script can run another. The child gets fresh memory, fresh variables and its own settings,
and shares nothing with its parent except the compiled code itself. Values passed between them
are copied, never handed over as a pointer into shared memory. Limits are counted against the
request that began the whole chain, so a script cannot escape its budget by spawning more work,
and a child never holds more permission than its parent.
